history: Autódromo Internacional Zilmar Beux de Cascavel, located in Paraná, Brazil, has been a cornerstone of Brazilian motorsport since its inception. Initially a dirt track, it was paved in the 1970s, becoming a prominent venue for national racing series. The full circuit layout, a 3.033 km challenge, has hosted numerous significant events over the years, including rounds of the Brazilian Formula Truck championship and various touring car series. The track is named after Zilmar Beux, a local motorsport enthusiast who was instrumental in the circuit's development. Cascavel has consistently provided a platform for both established drivers and rising stars in Brazilian racing.
atmosphere: The air at Cascavel on race day is thick with anticipation. The roar of engines echoes off the grandstands as the Brazilian sun beats down, baking the asphalt. The smell of racing fuel and burning rubber hangs heavy, mingling with the scent of grilled meats from the numerous vendors surrounding the track. The passionate Brazilian fans, adorned in team colors, create an electric atmosphere, their cheers rising and falling with every overtake and near miss. The energy is palpable, creating a uniquely Brazilian racing experience.
trackCharacter: The Cascavel Full Circuit layout is a blend of high-speed straights and technical corners. It demands a car that's both powerful and nimble. The long straights reward horsepower, but the series of flowing corners require precise handling and a well-balanced chassis. The track's relatively flat profile contributes to consistent grip levels, but also puts a premium on mechanical grip, as there are few camber changes to aid cornering. The circuit flows well, rewarding commitment and precision.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Lago
famousCorners.description: A fast, sweeping left-hander that requires commitment and carries a lot of speed onto the back straight.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining a consistent line and carrying maximum speed through the corner without running wide.

famousCorners.name: Curva da Ferradura
famousCorners.description: A tight hairpin that demands heavy braking and precise turn-in.
famousCorners.challenge: Balancing braking and steering to avoid locking up or running wide on the exit.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Miolo
famousCorners.description: A complex of medium-speed corners in the middle sector that tests a car's handling and driver's precision.
famousCorners.challenge: Stringing together the sequence of corners perfectly to maintain momentum and avoid scrubbing speed.

famousCorners.name: Reta dos Boxes
famousCorners.description: The main straight, offering a prime overtaking opportunity with the aid of DRS.
famousCorners.challenge: Maximizing top speed and slipstreaming to get alongside the car ahead before the braking zone for Curva do Lago.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Trevo
famousCorners.description: A long right-hander that leads onto the main straight and requires a good exit to maximize speed.
famousCorners.challenge: Getting on the power early without losing traction, and positioning the car for a clean run down the straight.

overtakingSpots: Reta dos Boxes (into Curva do Lago)
historySnippets: Cascavel was initially a dirt track before being paved.
The circuit is named after Zilmar Beux, a key figure in its development.
The Brazilian Formula Truck series has been a regular feature at Cascavel.
Cascavel is located in the state of Paraná, in southern Brazil.
The circuit's relatively flat layout means mechanical grip is crucial.
The 'Curva do Lago' is one of the fastest and most challenging corners on the track.
weatherNotes: Cascavel experiences a humid subtropical climate. Rain is common, especially during the summer months (December to March), which can make the track extremely slippery. Even in dry conditions, humidity can affect tire grip and engine performance. Temperatures can range from mild to hot, adding to the physical demands on drivers.
drivingAdvice: At Cascavel, focus on maximizing corner exit speed, especially out of Curva do Trevo onto the main straight. Precision is key in the Miolo section; stringing together the corners smoothly will pay dividends in lap time. Be aggressive on the brakes into Curva da Ferradura, but avoid locking up, as the exit is critical. Set up your car for mechanical grip, as the track lacks significant elevation changes. Protect your tires, as the abrasive surface can lead to degradation during longer races.
famousRaces: Brazilian Formula Truck Championship: Cascavel has hosted many memorable races in this series, known for its spectacular crashes and close battles.
Stock Car Brasil: Cascavel has been a regular fixture on the Stock Car Brasil calendar, showcasing some of Brazil's best touring car drivers.
Local Touring Car Series: The circuit has also hosted numerous regional and national touring car championships, providing a platform for local talent.
localCulture: Cascavel is a vibrant city in the western part of Paraná state, known for its agricultural industry and friendly people. The local cuisine features hearty dishes with beef, pork, and corn as staple ingredients. Churrasco (Brazilian barbecue) is a must-try, and the local beer is a perfect complement. Paddock life is relaxed and welcoming, with a strong sense of community among the teams and drivers. The locals are passionate about motorsport and eager to share their culture with visitors.
